title: Living Your Life As A Hireling

sense.text:
“His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” This is the white man. His bones are filled with the sins of his youth. You can go back to Cain, when God said Cain would be a fugitive and a vagabond. That is talking about his descendants. A fugitive is somebody always running from justice, and the white man has never been judged yet.

Even now the ICC put out a warrant for Netanyahu’s arrest, and Trump said Netanyahu has nothing to fear, he is not going to be arrested. They don’t give a damn what the international court says.

That is what we are dealing with: Esau trying to destroy the business of Nolan Wells’ mother, nations who don’t even know each other all coming to the defense of white supremacy; a black officer who drowned saving his fiancée, and none of the white cops there jumped in or will speak on behalf of the brother; don’t fall for white women’s tears; a 17-year-old black boy shot dead by three cops on an Austin playground over a water bottle, and the police chief blaming the kid. All you got to be is black, and that’s a threat.

“Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth”: he loves wickedness. “Though he hide it under his tongue”: he hid that wickedness for about sixty years, from the civil rights era up until this new administration. In that time you saw a new America. They loved black and brown people; we got jobs; we reached the height of government; you even had President Barack Hussein Obama, and everybody said he’s our Moses.

Then the new administration came in and said, You’re fired. DEI, get out. Affirmative action no more, and Clarence Thomas said, Yes, boss. Over 3,000 black women in high-ranking positions were fired within months, and Howard University dropped 52 incoming freshmen. This is not a new America. It is the old America coming back. Making America great is what’s great for them and bad for us.

“Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth”: it is still there. Our people say, No, they’re not like that, I know them, these are good white folks, I just got a promotion, they helped me get a discount on a new car, don’t talk about the white man like that. But the wickedness is still within his mouth.

precepts.why:
“Never trust thine enemy.” God says never trust him: “for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” The same way iron rusts, that is how his wickedness is, and it will surely come to pass.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: he is nice to you. You got that promotion you wanted, that house at a discount, everything you wanted; he comes crouching to you, I’m sorry for this, I’m sorry for that. “Yet take good heed and beware of him.” When you wipe a lookingglass that had dust on it, you can see through it, and “thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The rust is his wickedness. It is still there, hidden under the tongue just as Job says.

“Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place.” That is what happened historically. We set them by us at the end of the dark ages, and they conquered us and took our place as Jews and Christians.

The record shows it. The Cambridge History of Judaism, covering 1500 to 1815, says new information about Jewish communities, or imagined Jewish communities, in sub-Saharan Africa came chiefly from Arab historians and geographers. Those Arab geographers were present at the time, and they were black, Jews that spoke Arabic. Esau found their records of black Jewish communities and wrote in the word imagined. Leo Africanus was one of our people, an ambassador of high status who was enslaved, renamed, and used for his photographic memory to chart where the Jews were throughout Africa so they could enslave us.

John Pory wrote that the Abyssines affirm that west of the Nile there dwelt a most populous nation of the Jewish stock under a mighty king, and the cosmographers marked a province between Abyssinia and Congo called the land of the Hebrews. John Ogilby wrote in 1670 that on the coast of Guinea many Jews were scattered, natives boasting themselves of Abraham’s seed on both sides of the river Niger, others who fled from the desolation of Jerusalem by Vespasian. By the 18th century there were many accounts of the lost tribes of Israel along the western coast of Africa, and a Scottish explorer described Arabic-speaking Jews in West Africa and many Jews near Timbuktu, whose descendants, now Muslims, still invoke their Jewish origins.

They got many of the slaves from that coast of West Africa. Those aren’t the only Israelites, but it shows we know we are the Israelites, biblically and historically. That is why we don’t have time to argue with Christians about the Trinity.

sense.text:
Marriage is political, and it generally reveals where your allegiance is. Everybody got excited when Jamie Foxx wore a shirt saying Jesus is a black man, and then out comes his Australian girlfriend.

Remember the history of Balaam and Balak. Balaam said, God will not allow me to curse the 12 tribes, but I have a plan: if the women of Moab get among these Israelite men, those women can cause the men to worship their gods, and then you have a chance to defeat them. That is what happened. So Moses said, “Have ye saved all the women alive? Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.” These are the women that got us to sin.

So watch these black actors who get a non-black woman, or one they call exotic, racially ambiguous. When they open their mouth, they are certain they ain’t black. Watch out for them; they will do you dirty. A man like Brandon Tatum will say marriage isn’t political, and he will kill black people if he gets a chance. He hates his people. In the 50s Esau was saying the Bible says no miscegenation, no racial mixing, and black people got mad. The Bible does say that. What are you mad for?
Gamaliel, the Pharisee and doctor of the law, is the one that taught and instructed Paul.

Gamaliel goes through some history here, and the fuller account is in the complete works of Flavius Josephus. Theudas rose up “boasting himself to be somebody”, and Judas of Galilee “drew away much people after him.” These two men set themselves up to be somebody, and both were put to death, because their intent was to go against the laws of the land, and all that obeyed them were scattered.
“All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.”
“I am the door”: by Christ a man shall enter and “find pasture”, and that pasture is the kingdom.

Who is the thief? Rome. “The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy.” Rome stole, Rome did a whole lot of killing, and Rome destroyed us. Christ came “that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.”
The hireling “seeth the wolf coming”: he sees danger coming, and he “leaveth the sheep, and fleeth.” He runs for his life, and the wolf catcheth them and scattereth the sheep.

“The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.” A brother that is a hireling does not care for the sheep.

A hireling is a worker employed purely for monetary gain. He is only there to get what he can get from the body. He lacks loyalty to the cause; a hireling has no loyalty, and 2018 showed us that. There are still hirelings among us. He is willing to do unpleasant or unethical work just for a paycheck. He is a mercenary, he cares only about the cold hard cash, and he has no passion for the work. He is the one a boss uses for dirty work.

That is where the dead spirits come from. The brothers with dead spirits are hirelings. They have no passion for this truth; they could care less. This is the Buena Vista Social Club for them, a hangout: I ain’t got nothing else to do, they got some pretty women over there.

The pastors in the sitdown with Fred Price Jr. are hirelings too. In that sitdown the captain asked how we are going to clean our people up, the hookers, the drug dealers, the killings, by arguing about the Trinity or by teaching God’s commandments, and where the black church’s voice is on the atrocities done to our people. Them pastors went right back to the Trinity. They don’t give a damn about our people.

This is a class of self-examination: how do you know if you are a hireling?

precepts.why:
“Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?” A dispensation of time is given to every man on this earth, and his days are his life.

“As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work.” A hireling generally looks for the reward of his work. That is what he is looking for, and that is why he flees when the wolf comes: he is there for the reward, not for the sheep.

sense.text:
Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. “Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them by sending them to the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the Holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the 12 tribes of Israel.

Even in the time of Christ we were scattered into groups: the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians. It is happening today. This is not so much talking about Esau; it is talking about our people, the Israelites.
The Lord God of who? “The Lord God of Israel.” “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites, the 12 tribes.
God will gather the remnant of his flock out of all countries “and will bring them again to their folds”, back to their tribes, “and they shall be fruitful and increase.”

“And I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them.” Not feeding them with jumping up and down, screaming, foaming at the mouth and rolling around on the floor. They feed them with knowledge and understanding of God’s laws.

“Neither shall they be lacking.” Right now we are a lacking people. We lack knowledge, wisdom and understanding. Broken down, we lack rulership, we lack dominion of the earth, we lack our own country, we lack a fortified family, we lack a nation. We are lacking everything.
“I will raise unto David a righteous Branch”: this is Christ, the King that shall reign and execute judgment and justice in the earth.
“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely”: remember, we were split into two kingdoms, and both are saved in his days.

“The north country” is North America. And God leads the seed of the house of Israel out of all countries, “and they shall dwell in their own land.” That is what we are lacking: we don’t have our own land.
Jeremiah is speaking: “Mine heart within me is broken because of the prophets.”
“For the land is full of adulterers.”
“For both prophet and priest are profane; yea, in my house have I found their wickedness.” In God’s own house he found the prophets and priests were wicked.
“Their way shall be unto them as slippery ways in the darkness”: whatever path they took, they would fall. “I will bring evil upon them”: God brought the Babylonians on them.
Samaria is the northern kingdom. They “prophesied in Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.” It was the same with the northern kingdom as well.

“They commit adultery.” A woman who answered the church’s official phone for months found the pastor used that number to set up meetings with women. Look how the women dress in church now; back in the day you could never walk into church like that. You may say that is AI, but that stuff is real. I grew up in the church and saw all kinds of things.

“And walk in lies”, like the pastors in the sitdown, whose whole point was not to keep God’s commandments.

“They strengthen also the hands of evildoers.” A pastor gave a white family $50,000 for driving from the west coast of Canada to join his church. Like the movie Leap of Faith, with people planted in the audience. They don’t do that for black people. Where is that in the scriptures? Peter told the man asking for money he had no silver and gold.

“That none doth return from his wickedness”: that pastor is not turning from nothing. “They are all of them unto me as Sodom”: a woman in church celebrating twenty years married to another woman. “And the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah”: a man in a dress preaching in a black church in Atlanta. These black churches got to go.

“I will feed them with wormwood”: destruction, death. “And make them drink the water of gall”: poison. “For from the prophets of Jerusalem is profaneness gone forth into all the land”: it is talking about our people.

“They make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart”, meaning their own mind, what they feel at that moment. These are the people on TikTok and Instagram saying, I don’t know who this is for, but God has a message for you, and it is something they went through the night before. “And not out of the mouth of the Lord”: what they say is not coming from the Bible, not from the scriptures.

“They say still unto them that despise me”: they are talking to people that really hate God, and if you speak to Christians you will find a lot of them really hate God.

“The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace.” In the sitdown, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, the church won’t be here. Christians just lie and tell you there will be peace and no problems. “No evil shall come upon you”: ain’t nothing bad going to happen to us. They walk “after the imagination of his own heart”, after their own mind.

“For who hath stood in the counsel of the Lord?” Who stood in the word of God? That is the issue. Nobody is standing in the counsel of the Lord; they are going after the imagination and thoughts of their own mind.

“The anger of the Lord shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the thoughts of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.” That is what we read in Deuteronomy 4: tribulation shall come in the latter days.

Our people will not repent unless they get a foot up their behind. Death makes people reconsider their ways. In the Old Testament, when Israel would not hear, God said kill them, and that made all Israel fear. Today God says to the white man, kill this many of them, and our people say, Why? We’re Christians, we serve the same God you do. And the white man says, We don’t give a damn about that.

A 16-year-old black girl was found tied to a tree by her neck with a ratchet strap, and they called it suicide. A 27-year-old woman and the 16-year-old girl were both found hanging from trees and both ruled suicides, and there is a whole list of names like them. They can insult our intelligence like that because we are not unified. We are not connected to the Lord, we are not organized, and there is no consequence; they say a few things on the news, and then the 4th of July or Christmas comes and everyone forgets. They are not only coming for the men. All you independent women who say you don’t see color: color sees you.

“I have not sent these prophets”: these pastors, these Christian reverends. “Yet they ran”: I’m going to build a church here. “I have not spoken to them”: when they say God spoke to me, it is a lie, and the scripture shows how you know it is a lie.

“But if they had stood in my counsel”: if they had stayed in the Bible, “and had caused my people to hear my words”, let the people hear what the word of God says, “then they should have turned them from their evil way.” With the word of God you can turn the people from their evil way. That is what the captains were doing in that sitdown: turning the minds of the people around. You can only transform them with the Bible, the commandments of God. That sitdown is going to reach millions, and the people that trusted in those pastors will see their pastors don’t know a thing.

“Saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.” Where does that come from? Martin Luther King. But did it really come from Martin Luther King? Stanley Levison, a Jewish businessman and lawyer, was one of King’s closest advisers. He raised his money, handled his finances and his books, and helped draft the I have a dream address. That was Amalek. When King spoke against the Vietnam war, his backers stopped giving him money. Zionist Jewish backers were behind him, manipulating everything, even that dream. They didn’t love us.

A brother in the class added that King in his heart wanted to do right by his people. He lived in a time when you could be lynched any moment, and he had to dance with the devil to get a little liberty. Still, the cracker wrote I have a dream. When your coffee is too black, too strong, you integrate it with cream and make it weak: it used to be hot and becomes cool; it used to wake you up and now it puts you to sleep.

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” This is where God drove the flock that he now gathers out of all countries.

We are scattered under these wood gods, like Christianity and the old wooden cross with its many denominations; Islam with its several denominations; even Judaism. Our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, and that is the scattering the hireling pastors keep up.

“And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.” That is what the shepherds God sets up feed the flock with: knowledge and understanding of God’s laws. Not jumping up and down, screaming and foaming at the mouth.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: flee from North America, because that is the land of the north. “For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: we are not just in North America, we are spread abroad.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” That is Judah. “For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: we are God’s favorite.

So the north country of Jeremiah 23:8 is North America, and the Lord leads the seed of Israel out of it and out of all countries into their own land.

The pastor in the sitdown kept saying we are not going to be in the tribulation. But Paul and Barnabas were “confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The only way we enter the kingdom of God is through much tribulation. So what Bible are these Christians reading? They are not reading the scripture, and that is the lie of “Ye shall have peace.”

“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen.” There we serve “gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.”

“But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”: in all the lands we were scattered to, if we seek the Lord our God he shall be found, “if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul”, meaning do everything God says, his commandments and his laws.

And when? “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days.” So these Christians don’t know what they are talking about. Israel is in tribulation in the latter days, and the way out is to “turn to the Lord thy God” and “be obedient unto his voice.”

Read verse 13 first: “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was the time of Adam.

Then Ezra says, “thou hast ordained in thy law, that the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide.” The strait things are tribulation, and the wide is what was in the elder world. “For they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.”

So all Israel is going through tribulation, the righteous and the unrighteous. What we are seeing on the news, death after death, is just the beginning, and it is going to escalate. They are not going to ask what God you serve or what religion you are. You are in the image of God, a melanated brother or sister, and that is enough. It is going to happen to all the 12 tribes.

How do you know it is a lie when they say God spoke to them? Miriam said she was a prophet too, and she was. But God said, “If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.”

“My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house. With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches.” The only one the Lord spoke with mouth to mouth was Moses. Moses could say God told me this.

So when you hear black women say God told me this morning, his voice was so clear, that is a lie. He didn’t speak to you. He only spoke to Moses like that. That is the prophet God never spoke to, who prophesies anyway.

Martin Luther King integrated, and the Amalekites around him wrote his dream. “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”: God is telling us to separate from these nations, these unbelievers.

“And touch not the unclean thing”: don’t follow their customs, their religions, their holidays, their politics. “And I will receive you”: only then will God receive us, “and will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.”

This is where Paul’s instruction came from. God instructed the 12 tribes to separate from the other nations and stop following their customs and traditions: “And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.”

So what Paul taught in Corinthians is nothing new. The churches never taught you that. All churches want to integrate, like the pastor who made it sound so moving to say this is not a black church. He didn’t have to dance with the devil. He sounds like the devil.

sense.text: What Jeremiah prophesied is very similar to what Ezekiel prophesied: “prophesy against the shepherds of Israel.” “Should not the shepherds feed the flocks?”

“Ye eat the fat”, “ye clothe you with the wool”: they get the best clothes. “Ye kill them that are fed”, the sheep and the goats, “but ye feed not the flock.” You ain’t taking care of the flock; you are feeding yourself.

“Neither have ye brought again that which was driven away”: the 12 tribes that were scattered. “Neither have ye sought that which was lost.” “But with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them”: that is how they ruled the 12 tribes at that time. Assyria had already come, Babylon came, and Ezekiel is in the Babylonian captivity.
“They became meat to all the beasts of the field”: they became meat to all the nations.

We were scattered in all countries and lands: “my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them.” None of these pastors are searching or seeking for the 12 tribes.

And there are Israelite groups that are not seeking or searching for the 12 tribes either. They are comfy at home on the internet, comfy standing on the corner with nobody listening to them, and their whole campaign is trying to stop the Israelites that are actually doing the work and trying to save our people. That is how demonic they are.
“Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” That I is Christ. That is what Christ was doing, what Paul and the apostles were doing, and that was the great commission.
He will deliver them out of “all places”: all countries, all lands where they have been scattered.

“And I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries.” The Most High sends both the angels and the prophets to gather the 12 tribes. There is no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors.
“I will feed them in a good pasture”: that is the kingdom, upon the high mountains of Israel.
“I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down”: we are going to be at rest.

“I will seek that which was lost”: that is our people. Our people were driven away, we were broken, and we are the sick ones. “But I will destroy the fat and the strong; I will feed them with judgment”: God is going to destroy the nations.

As we read this we have to examine ourselves. Are we in this truth with loyalty? Do we have a passion for this truth, or are we just here? Am I here because you’re my buddy, and wherever he goes I go? That is how some brothers are. Your relationship has to be by the Bible. The Bible is the link; without the Bible there is no link.

precepts.why: “But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That proves the I in Ezekiel 34:11 is Christ. He is the one who searches his sheep and seeks them out, and he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

“He shall call to the heavens from above”: those are the angels. “And to the earth”: the earth is the prophets, you and me on the earth. “That he may judge his people.”

“Gather my saints together unto me”: that is the message to the angels and to the prophets. “Those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: that is the 12 tribes of Israel. So he tells the prophets, gather the 12 tribes, and he tells the angels, gather the 12 tribes. That is the gathering of Ezekiel 34:13.

They say Christ said gather everybody, all people. No. “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” The angels gather his elect, the same gathering Ezekiel saw.

Who are the elect? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect are Israel. So the angels in Matthew 24 gather Israel from the four winds, just as Ezekiel 34 says God will gather his flock from the countries. There is no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old; the contradiction comes from the hireling pastors.

“Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints. Let Israel rejoice in him that made him.” We have not been rejoicing in our creator; we have been rejoicing in the white man. “Let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: we must be joyful in our King and his kingdom, because for so long we have been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people.” He doesn’t take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people. “He will beautify the meek with salvation.”

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That is the rest. Singing aloud upon their beds is the lying down of Ezekiel 34:15: God feeds his flock and causes them to lie down.

sense.text:
“Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee.” These prophets are the hirelings: the hireling pastors and the hireling Israelites. You can count down the vain and foolish things they have seen: there is going to be peace, there is going to be love, you can marry white women, you can have 15 wives in the midst of poverty, God accepts it all. Give your tithe, 10% of your check every week. Let me lay hands on you, Sister Betty. Lie, lie, lie.

“And they have not discovered thine iniquity.” They never said the reason blacks and Latinos are in captivity and suffer oppression is because we break God’s commandments. The reason we suffer is our sins, and they never tell us that. Instead they say, This is your season; donate $1,000 to me and you’ll get $10,000 by the end of the year. All lies.

“To turn away thy captivity”: we went into captivity because of our sins, and that is why Christ had to come and die on the cross to save us from our sins.

“But have seen for thee false burdens and causes of banishment.” A false burden is something you don’t have to carry, but you carry it anyway: Christmas, spending the whole check on gifts; a new suit, new shoes and new drawers every Easter; New Year’s Eve; wedding anniversaries; Valentine’s Day; Thanksgiving. God never said, Today is my birthday, what are you going to buy me? By supporting those false burdens we are banished from the coming kingdom, banished from New Jerusalem.

“For though I preach the gospel”: all you brothers preach the gospel, and you sisters with children are preaching the gospel to them. “For necessity is laid upon me”: we want to save our lives, we want the coming Jerusalem. “Yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!”

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward”: if you do this willingly, you have a passion for this truth and loyalty to God Almighty, and you have a reward.

“But if against my will”: somebody always has to yell at me and tell me to do this and that, because I am a hireling. I am not really in this to go out and teach the gospel. You hear how boring I am, the dead spirit on me; I could care less.

“A dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me”: you get a limited amount of time in this truth, and then God moves you out of the way and brings somebody else. A brother in the class added that it is musical chairs: over the years we have seen whole new congregations come before us: same spirits, different people. Facebook shows you memories from two years ago and you ask, who are these brothers I was standing with? It is all new people, because those dudes fell out.

“Go to law before the unjust”: the law here is the Pharisees, not Rome. Rome was not listening to every little problem among us. The Pharisees were the unjust, “and not before the saints”: the saints were the followers of Christ.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The Pharisees aren’t judging anything; the saints that follow Christ shall judge the world. That is our reward to come. Christ is saying through Paul: judge the smallest matters among you. Stop going to the scribes and Pharisees, and deal with the saints among you that follow Christ and know the scriptures.
“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” We shall judge the leaders. You are not judging Michael and Gabriel; that is not what it is talking about.
“Set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church”: the least esteemed are the young men, the lower-ranked men.

“I speak to your shame.” Paul is trying to shame the leaders in Corinth, because they are not doing their job. “Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?” Are you all a bunch of idiots? You have all this rank, and “not one that shall be able to judge between his brethren.”

It is the same today. When we visited California I asked the brothers questions and heard some of the most outrageous answers; they don’t study. In the war room, brothers come in and sit silent; you don’t know they are in the room until they leave. Why does that happen? Because you’re a hireling. There is no true loyalty and no true passion. It is a club, a hangout.

So Paul was saying: raise up the least esteemed, the lower ranks, and use them. Stop wasting your time with brothers that have been around you ten years and aren’t doing anything. They lack the zeal and the fire; you have to force them to do everything. Turn to the young men who have zeal, who want to learn and grow, who have questions and fire when the scripture is read. Let the others sit in the back and fade away.

Another Bishop added that you really see it on the quests in the middle of the ocean: there is nothing else to do, and still those brothers are never around. To them it is a vacation.

precepts.why: “Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.” That is the law right there. The scribes and Pharisees were the law, so the unjust that Paul says not to go to law before are the Pharisees, not Rome.

Who are the angels the saints shall judge? “Ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” It is not Michael, Gabriel and Uriel. It is talking about our own people, the leaders of the 12 tribes.

sense.text: “They thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.” A lot of men and women thought the kingdom was coming at that time. That is why Paul warned that that day would not come until there came a falling away first and the man of sin was revealed.
“A certain nobleman went into a far country”: in this context the far country is the heavens, where Christ went “to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.”
“Occupy till I come.” The pounds he delivered to his servants are God’s word.

“But his citizens hated him.” Who hated him? He came unto his own and his own received him not: the scribes and Pharisees and those that followed them. Today there are no groups called scribes and Pharisees, but the Christians and the Muslims fall into this.
“How much every man had gained by trading”: gained by going out and teaching the word.
“Have thou authority over ten cities.” That is what we all want: dominion.

“Be thou also over five cities.” One city is too much to handle in this body and mind we have now. Can you imagine five cities, ten cities? The Lord is going to have to change us, because some of you have problems dealing with the one woman you have right now.

“Here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” That is the hireling. I kept it laid up; I didn’t do anything with the knowledge you bestowed on me, the faith you gave me. When you ask these brothers and sisters about it, they have an excuse.

“Thou art an austere man”: a strict man. “Thou takest up that thou layedst not down”: Christ is collecting Israel. He is not on the earth teaching with us anymore; he is watching us from the heavens, and he is coming to collect.
“Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.” Your excuses will not fly with Christ. He calls him a wicked servant; he doesn’t care about your excuses.
“The bank” is the congregation. “Usury” means interest: when Christ comes back, he wants interest on what he gave each of us.

“And he said unto them that stood by”: these are the soldiers, the men around the throne. Imagine a king giving orders to the men next to the throne, like in Game of Thrones. It is not going to be a crowd; it is pure order.

“From him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.” His one pound was supposed to make him lord over one city, and it is taken from him. A brother in the class added: we have seen brothers come among us with certain skills who did not expand on them, so the Most High, in the musical chairs, moved them out of the way. Other brothers came in, took that office and ran with it, and you hear nothing of the men who had the ability.

“But those mine enemies” goes right back to verse 14: “We will not have this man to reign over us.” “Bring hither, and slay them before me”: he tells the soldiers around him to bring them before him and kill them. The churches won’t read that in Sunday school, but that is what it says.

It means you are not going to be able to just do what you want. You were put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don’t do it there is no reason for you to live. If you don’t want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

precepts.why: “He was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” That is when Christ left, the nobleman going into a far country. The two men in white apparel said, “this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.” He went to heaven to receive the kingdom, and he is coming back.
“Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold.” The pounds Christ delivered to his servants to occupy with are God’s word, his commandments, worth more than gold.

The citizens that hated him are the ones who rejected him: “the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.” Highlight “rejected”: the elders, chief priests and scribes are the citizens who said “We will not have this man to reign over us.”

“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers.” That is the authority over ten cities.

We are not going to play with the nations, because we have to teach them to honor the King of kings. We will teach them the civil law, the ceremonial law, the dietary law and the moral law, and it will be done through force. We will teach them the history of Israel too. They won’t be glorifying China, or the Hamites, or the white man anymore; they will glorify the history of Israel.

“Not slothful in business”: this is God’s business. If it were the white man’s business you wouldn’t be slothful, because you have to eat and have a place to live. “Fervent in spirit”: on fire in your spirit, “serving the Lord.” The servant who laid up his pound in a napkin was slothful in God’s business.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” Bearing no fruit means no fruits of the spirit. You’re the same grimy negro you were five years back: no change, no evolution, no transformation in you. It goes for men and women: the same gossiper, murmurer and complainer you were five years ago, just here with the fringes and the border of blue. He taketh it away; he kills you.

“And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” You are growing, and you have to be purged to bring forth more fruit. Cut this off, cut that person off from you, cut this out of your soul and spirit so you can bear more fruit.

He laid it up in a napkin, and when you ask brothers, and sisters too, about it, that is what they do: “A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” That is the hireling. For every solution these people have five excuses and five problems.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The bank is his great house, the congregation.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use.” So your work, your love, your zeal and your understanding: bring it into the bank, into the congregation, and Christ will require it with usury when he comes.

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” “Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name?” “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

That goes back to what we just read. This man was in the truth and took his pound and hid it in a napkin: I’m not helping them anymore; I did it full time, but I don’t want to do it no more. He will say he preached in Christ’s name, and Christ will say I never knew you.

A hireling has a temporary time in this truth, men and women. They don’t care about salvation. They are willing to destroy their family, the brotherhood, everything they built up, for their own sin, the love of sin. “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Moses chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” Anybody who says sin isn’t pleasurable is lying; it is very fun, but you have to abstain. The hireling who hid his pound chose the pleasures of sin for a season over suffering with the people of God.
“That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” Pleasure in unrighteousness is what draws the hireling away from the truth, and it ends in damnation.

sense.text:
Here is another type of hireling: Diotrephes. “I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” The apostles set him up, and he made it appear he was in the truth.

You see brothers who put in no works, and then they hear there is a congregation in Alaska with no senior man there. I’m in the office of ten, I have a bright idea; I won’t ask counsel from anybody, I’ll just pop up and say I’m over the congregation, and because I come from the States they’ll love and accept me. That generally happens. It happened in Ghana and in many African countries. Another brother went out there, and when the brothers asked where the congregation’s donations were, the money was in his personal bank account.

These are hirelings. They don’t believe; there is no fear among them. Everybody’s problem isn’t always sex. Some brothers want power, preeminence: I was never anything in the world, so I’m going to come in and be somebody, not by the word of God, but by being deceitful, slick and witty, disrespectful in a secretive way. He was disrespectful to the apostles: he “receiveth us not.”

“If I come, I will remember his deeds”: I’m going to remember this negro. “Prating against us with malicious words”: he always has something smart to say. He ain’t nobody, I know what he knows, I know more precepts than you. We have been down that road before.

“Neither doth he himself receive the brethren”: none of the brothers were allowed in. “And forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church”: if anybody says, I want to go visit the apostles, then don’t come back; you’re not welcome anymore.

precepts.why:
There is only one preeminent, and that is Christ. He is the King, not you, not me. “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.”

Christ has the preeminence, not Diotrephes. Diotrephes lost his mind because he was a hireling.

sense.text:
“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign is to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? He was raised up, and the word was: Don’t raise that negro up, he ain’t right. To walk feignedly is to be a fake brother, pretending. It includes pretending an illness, and a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick; faking an emotion; making up an excuse.

“But remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

This is where you examine yourself. Am I a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you and God know the answer; we don’t. If a sister asks us about a brother, we can only tell her what he shows us, how he portrays himself. Whether he is really like that, she has to talk with him more personally to find out how he truly is.

precepts.why:
Some brothers can fake it really well. “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.”

There is going to be a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another. It is going to happen because the scriptures say so. But we must be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. In the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, and we expect the same today. Some of them are sitting here right now.
“No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That is a hireling. He walks feignedly, puts his hand to the work, and looks back.

“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the man who put his pound in the napkin: he drew back.

Sometimes you can see it. In the restructuring we called captains and asked, why did you move this brother from this position? He’s not the same anymore. When he came in he was on fire; we didn’t have to tell him what to do. Now you have to yell at him and force him. So we drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

When brothers are moved and start to weep and howl, they were not here for the sincerity of this gospel; they were here for a position, to be over these men. This is how we have to be: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That is the opposite of walking feignedly.

“Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When the scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to burn: how do I get this word out, how am I going to teach, what ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else doesn’t matter.

If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you have no desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself and to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You’re a hireling. You could be here five, ten, twenty years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out.

“Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Faith unfeigned: not fake, not folly. That is the opposite of those that have walked feignedly.

“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don’t be fake, don’t be phony with the brethren.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another; Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God’s work. “Fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit, “serving the Lord.” That is the brother who does not walk feignedly.

sense.text: “Behold, I, even I, will judge between the fat cattle and between the lean cattle.” That goes with what Christ said in the New Testament, that all nations shall be before him and he shall separate the sheep from the goats. It comes from here.

“Therefore will I save my flock, and they shall no more be a prey.” We are prey to our own people. A lot of times we think of being prey only to the nations, but our own people prey upon us as well: p-r-e-y, not p-r-a-y.
“And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David.”
“And I will make with them a covenant of peace”: that is why he is the Prince of Peace.
“There shall be showers of blessing”: blessings upon blessings.
“The earth shall yield her increase.” Remember God told Cain the earth would not yield him her strength. Here the earth yields her strength to us.
“And they shall no more be a prey to the heathen”: the other nations. “None shall make them afraid”: nobody will ever make us afraid again, because right now we live in fear.
“A plant of renown”: renown means famous.
This chapter deals with going to the left or right of what God says. If God tells us something, let us follow it and follow the Lamb wherever he goes. Jeroboam was the head of the northern kingdom.
“Lay hold on him”: grab that man of God. And his hand “dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.” His arm shriveled up.

“Intreat now the face of the Lord thy God.” You see how pain will get you to change your thoughts. A few minutes earlier he wanted to put the man to death; now he wants him to pray to God for him. And the king’s hand was restored.
“For so was it charged me by the word of the Lord.” The Lord instructed him what not to do and what to do.
There dwelt an old prophet in Bethel, and his sons saw what happened between the man of God and Jeroboam and went and told their father.
“I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord.” “But he lied unto him.” “So he went back with him”: the prophet of Judah went back with the northern kingdom.
“The sepulchre of thy fathers”: the graveyard.

Remember what we read earlier: the only one God speaks with mouth to mouth is Moses; everybody else he speaks to in dreams and visions. This old prophet said an angel came to him and told him to bring the prophet back to eat and drink, and he lied. “It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord.” That is why you have to be mindful with brothers.

“Made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places”: Jeroboam made bums priests: hump back, one eye, one leg. “Whosoever would, he consecrated him”: whoever wanted to be a priest, he made him a priest. “And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off.”

That is why the Lord said to put no trust in a brother, for every brother will utterly supplant. Some people are in your life for blessings and some for cursings, and ultimately it is to try each and every one of us.
